executiveSummary: GM0946's 2025 identity, generalized boundary, contained reference point, 17,512 residents, fifteen neighbourhoods, four BAG places, eighteen BRT settlements and three logical road-border links are internally coherent; all ten canonical presets also execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Nederweert's real hazard geography is structured by the Zuid-Willemsvaart, Kanaal Wessem-Nederweert, Noordervaart, Neerpeelbeek and local watercourses, and by drought-sensitive peat, heath and woodland at De Groote Peel and Weerterbos. Municipal planning explicitly maps separate high- and low-priority pluvial areas, blocked-through-road risk, storage/overflow, heat and drought-sensitive nature-fire areas. Waterschap Limburg documents recurring heavy-rain inundation around Bientje north of the Noordervaart and a culvert path to the Neerpeelbeek, with 2025 works now in aftercare rather than proof of incident-time protection. The simulator instead publishes persistent generic major-river stress at T+24 and T+72—legacy depth field 0.753195, 1,913 rising to 2,311 affected residents and 87,036 rising to 355,296 person-hours—without selecting a connected Maas/canal/stream event, hydraulic boundary, defence/structure state, terrain footprint, arrival or recession. Pluvial T+24 likewise shows residual depth 0.186709, zero affected residents and 44,691 person-hours after rainfall is zero, without binding rain to the municipal priority map, roads, culverts, sewers, storage or controls. Nine active preset/component families reuse one seeded fifteen-neighbourhood surface rather than mechanism geometry. The canonical wildfire ignition is remote and yields only smoke in GM0946, while a controlled ignition inside Ospeldijk produces city fire 0.362249 and smoke 0.394695 but still zero affected residents and no source-contained local consequence. Public layers expose 189 partial water/wastewater objects, four current local Waterinfo observations, one indicative air station, provider territories, one Enexis planning sample, 37 antenna sites and eight education locations; none supplies live connectivity, capacity, backup or restoration. The graph captures N275 and N266 but not the external A2 junction dependency that provincial sources identify as a key gateway; N275's two boundary edges are one physical corridor, not independent capacity. There is no local rail station or acute hospital; St. Jans Gasthuis in Weert is about 5.6 km straight-line away. No inspected source publishes a governed municipality-wide emergency-support-site, staff, stock, fuel, shelter, care-acceptance or completed-action ledger. Exact first-72-hour services and recovery must remain synthetic or Unknown until an event, mechanism-specific footprint, operational lifeline state and confirmed actions/resources are bound; missing data is never zero, safe, open or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0946 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0946 as Nederweert in Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord, with 17,512 residents, density 175/km², 25.8% aged 65 or older and 2,493 one-person households. The reference point [5.760693869877192,51.29470449186766] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Fifteen neighbourhoods in five districts sum to 17,515 residents, three above the municipal control (+0.017%); published households total 7,775 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 4,515. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 17,512 without rewriting source observations.

Leveroy, Nederweert, Nederweert-Eind and Ospel are the four BAG places and none of their retained centres lies outside the generalized boundary. Eighteen BRT features comprise twelve buurtschappen and six woonkernen; they are settlement geometry, not separate population controls or emergency facilities.
District-heating and public-charging fields are null in all 15 neighbourhoods. Those values remain NoData rather than numeric zero or absence.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Provinciaal Risicoprofiel Limburg 2023–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Jaargang 2023, published online April 2024 for policy period 2023–2027; regional planning evidence; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The profile is a province-scale policy risk inventory, not a selected GM0946 incident or municipality consequence surface. It explicitly lists river flood, river-dike breach, nature fire, heatwave, extreme drought, cold wave, storm/wind, earthquake and extreme precipitation.
It also lists disruption of gas, electricity, drinking water, wastewater, communications and oil, cyberattack and incidents involving dangerous substances on roads, water, rail, pipelines and sites.

The authority says flood and nature-fire risk change in space and time and identifies better spatial/temporal treatment and a more dynamic profile as development needs. This supports mechanism-specific valid-time input, not one timeless municipality hash.

The profile was produced with municipalities, Waterschap Limburg, Rijkswaterstaat, WML, Waterschapsbedrijf Limburg, Enexis, TenneT, Gasunie, ProRail, KNMI, RIVM, telecom and acute-care partners; participation does not turn the regional scenario catalogue into operator telemetry.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Omgevingsvisie buitengebied Nederweert and climate-adaptation map
evidenceSources.edition: Adopted 20 July 2021; municipal planning/context record; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The vision describes an outer area of agricultural land, brook valleys and large Natura 2000/nature areas including De Groote Peel, Weerterbos and Sarsven en De Banen, plus dry and wet woodland and peat/heath/open-water mosaics.

Its climate map distinguishes high-priority water nuisance using T=10, 35.7 mm in 45 minutes; lower-priority Herwijnen 93 mm in 70 minutes; roads liable to blockage, water-board channels, high/middle/low storage, overflow, heat islands and drought-sensitive possible nature-fire areas.

The municipality says the system is still too oriented to rapid discharge, seeks retention/infiltration/delayed discharge, identifies berm ditches for road runoff and notes insufficient water availability during extreme drought. These are mechanism and planning statements, not incident-time capacity or protection.
The vision identifies dependence on stations in Weert/Roermond and the A2/N266/N275 regional road system, and explicitly requires water-robust accessibility for emergency services.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Project Bientje completion and local heavy-rain pathway
evidenceSources.edition: Published 29 June 2026; works performed in 2025, residual works and aftercare/monitoring described; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Bientje lies north of the Noordervaart and discharges through a culvert to the Neerpeelbeek. Waterschap research found surrounding land regularly inundated during heavy rainfall.

Works restored the bank/channel profile, replaced culverts, removed sand/silt, deepened parts of the bed and raised an adjacent path. This is direct evidence of a local pluvial/drainage mechanism absent from generic municipal depth.

The authority says the works limit the chance of water nuisance and have moved into aftercare, with a management, maintenance and monitoring plan being prepared. This lifecycle record is neither zero risk nor an observation of operability during a scenario.
No published page field supplies connected sewer/catchment topology, current blockage, power/backup, remaining capacity, crew state or a T+72 recession forecast.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord / Gemeente Nederweert / cross-border nature managers
evidenceSources.title: E05 — Natuurbrand Managementplan Weerterbos–Hugterheide public implementation context
evidenceSources.edition: Published 22 April 2026; 2025–2029 implementation programme; planning/lifecycle evidence; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Nederweert and partners across the Limburg–Noord-Brabant boundary signed a nature-fire management plan for Weerterbos and Hugterheide, demonstrating a specific western cross-boundary fire-management area.

The programme includes fire compartments, improved responder access and reduction of flammable vegetation. These are mitigation measures and planned works, not a live ignition, fuel-moisture surface, completed barrier state or response-time guarantee.

Municipal E03 separately identifies De Groote Peel near Ospel/Ospeldijk as a major peat/heath nature area and maps drought-sensitive nature-fire areas. Both eastern and western fuel landscapes must be represented rather than one remote canonical ignition.

Any flame, smoke, evacuation or access output requires ignition/time, eligible fuel, moisture, wind/plume, barriers, suppression actions and cross-boundary resource state; absent fields remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / PDOK, Provincie Limburg, ProRail, OVapi and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — A2/N275/N266 lifecycle, static mobility and cross-boundary acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Province project page inspected 3 September 2026; NWB-light 2026-08-01 and transport snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03, CC0; OVapi schedule 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 2026-07-03, CC0
supports: Three logical links reach Weert via N275, Someren via N266 and Peel en Maas via N275. The two N275 boundary links form one physical corridor; the graph contains no explicit external A2 junction/gateway state.

The province identifies the N275–A2/exit 39 connection as a central corridor, completed its capacity work in October 2025, and still records constraints and 2027 works at Randweg West and the N275–Eind rotonde. Project stage is valid-time context, not live incident throughput.

NWB distances 0.182–0.478 km and nominal values 150 are boundary-derived geometry and scenario-unit ceilings, not lanes, vehicles/hour, bridge capacity, evacuation throughput or travel time. N266 canal-crossing and A2-gateway common-cause state are not separately causal.

There is no ProRail station or RIVM acute-care point inside; 32 GTFS stop areas are schedule context. St. Jans Gasthuis in Weert is about 5.6 km straight-line from the reference point, but annual rooms/visits and distance do not prove route, staffing, surge, diversion, backup or acceptance.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards and Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Partial water-control/wastewater register and timestamped canal observations
evidenceSources.edition: HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z, CC BY-SA 4.0, contributor completeness variable; Waterinfo snapshot retrieved 2026-09-02T18:03:18Z, generally ten-minute observations, CC0 unless component states otherwise
supports: Full-resolution CBS containment assigns 189 HWH points to GM0946: 180 weirs, four surface-water pumps and five sewer pumps. All capacity fields are null and register status 'gerealiseerd' denotes existence, not live operation.

Named context includes Gemaal Rietbeek, Gemaal Neerpeelbeek and sewer pumps Nederweert, Ospel, Budschop, Eind and Leveroy. Points do not supply connectivity, catchment, direction, unit-compatible capacity, control, power/backup or restoration.

Four local Waterinfo records were current at snapshot time: Noordervaart discharge and water level at Nederweert-Eind plus two levels at Sluis 15/voedingskanaal. They are timestamped station observations, not a hydraulic surface, future hydrograph, flood footprint or scenario action.
Waterinfo is explicitly non-mission-critical public context and point coverage is incomplete. HWH contributor coverage is partial; unlisted assets and null values remain Unknown/NoData.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord, Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, Netbeheer Nederland, RDI, DUO and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Utility responsibilities, public registers, local observations and 72-hour preparedness semantics
evidenceSources.edition: VRLN current guidance inspected 3 September 2026; public deployment and Mijn Aansluiting point queries retrieved 2–3 September 2026; licence/cadence source-specific
supports: VRLN identifies Enexis for gas/electricity and WML for drinking water. Its current guidance says long outages require joint prioritisation of emergency power and may require municipal temporary drinking-water distribution; households are advised to hold four litres per person per day for three days. Guidance defines roles/actions, not a confirmed GM0946 activation or stock.

A Public Domain provider-territory query returns Enexis electricity and overlapping gas/water/media candidates at the reference point, while drainage returns no feature. Territory overlap/no-match reinforces that polygons are responsibility context, not complete address connectivity, topology, outage or restoration.

One postcode sample 6031AK maps to Enexis area NEDW and reports large-user planning values/queues and eleven projects, earliest 2028. It is not current load, emergency reserve, outage telemetry or a municipal total; the exact dataset licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns 37 sites/90 antennas and DUO eight education locations; registers do not establish coverage, backhaul, power/backup, occupancy, shelter role, stocks or staffing. One indicative RIVM air station reported PM2.5 6 µg/m³ at 2026-09-02T17:00Z; it is not a plume, forecast, exposure surface or T+72 value.

The deployment assigns zero local KNMI fixed weather stations, Waterinfo forecasts, acute-care locations, government-service points, NDW road situations and 365-day seismic origins. Each is scoped NoData, never normal weather/water, open roads, service availability or safety.

identity.summary: GM0946, Nederweert, Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord agree across generated and official 2025 sources.
notes: Feature ID, bundle code/name, province and safety-region membership are coherent.
The municipality reference point lies inside the generalized 2025 geometry.
Administrative edition, planning lifecycle, observation validity and synthetic scenario time remain separate.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is coherent, but canal/brook catchments, pluvial priority areas and peat/woodland fuel landscapes are absent from the consequence model.
notes: Use full-resolution geometry for evidence containment; the generalized boundary and centre are overview controls only.
Major-river/canal levels, local stream flooding, intense rain, drought supply and peat/woodland fire are distinct mechanisms.
Bientje–Noordervaart–Neerpeelbeek connectivity and De Groote Peel/Weerterbos fuel and barrier geometry must not be replaced by one municipality-wide scalar.

demography.summary: Resident population reconciles within normal CBS rounding and deterministic allocation preserves the municipal control.
notes: Published neighbourhood population is 17,515, three above the 17,512 control (+0.017%).
Reconciliation removes three residents deterministically without changing source rows.
Resident data exclude workers, visitors, road/canal users, responders and dynamic care or shelter occupancy.

regionalDetail.summary: All fifteen neighbourhoods are retained, but NoData fields and source-blind local hazard allocation limit operational use.
notes: District heating and charging are null in every neighbourhood and remain NoData.
Nederweert and Ospel dominate resident allocation, but population size is not mechanism exposure.
Official climate priority, water-path and nature-fire geometry does not drive local ordering.

settlements.summary: Four BAG places and eighteen BRT settlements preserve town, village and dispersed-rural context without inventing emergency roles.
notes: All four BAG place centres lie inside the generalized boundary.
BRT types are twelve buurtschappen and six woonkernen.
A settlement, school, fire-station symbol or visitor centre is not a confirmed support point; no governed public site/capacity catalogue was found.

transport.summary: Static N275/N266 and bus context is traceable, but the A2 gateway, canal crossing, route state and destinations are unresolved.
notes: Three logical edges reduce to two physical road families; the two N275 edges are series, non-additive links.
The province identifies the N275–A2 junction as critical, but it has no explicit gateway/closure object in GM0946's graph.
No local rail station and external acute care increase reliance on road/bus; geometry and schedules do not prove live availability or throughput.

emergencyContext.summary: Regional and local authorities define credible hazards and preparedness actions, but no selected GM0946 incident or complete T0–T+72 resource state exists.
notes: Nature-fire compartments, water works, road projects and climate adaptation are lifecycle/planning records, not current incident performance.
VRLN guidance identifies emergency-power prioritisation and possible drinking-water distribution, but not activated locations, stock, staff or completion.
Support sites, shelter/care acceptance, responders, vehicles, fuel, generators, water stocks and restoration actions remain Unknown.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at six checkpoints across all eight services for GM0946.
notes: Initial focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 31.80 seconds, tests 31.56 seconds.
Diagnostic all-preset run passed one file/two tests in 13.43 seconds, tests 13.22 seconds; controlled Ospeldijk ignition executed in 0.388 seconds.
Final focused audit:model passed one file/two tests in 29.87 seconds, tests 29.64 seconds.
Execution coverage is not physical, spatial, network, operational or recovery calibration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, resident/demand/delivery reconciliation, deterministic arithmetic and cumulative-burden invariants hold.
notes: All numeric outputs are finite and bounded; affected population is integral and no greater than 17,512.
Neighbourhood population reconciles exactly to the municipality and service demand/delivery sums reconcile at every tested frame.
Cumulative deprived person-hours are non-decreasing, but numerical validity does not make their local cause or magnitude observed.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A common seeded fifteen-neighbourhood surface replaces Nederweert's mechanism-specific water, fire, wind, heat, cyber and smoke geography.
notes: Nine active preset/component families reuse one local hazard-seed ordering rather than sampling their own evidence-backed footprint.
The river preset selects no Maas/canal/stream boundary or structure state, while pluvial output ignores the municipal priority/road-blockage map and Bientje pathway.
Moving the wildfire epicentre into Ospeldijk creates city fire 0.362249 and smoke 0.394695 at T+24 but zero affected residents; the containing neighbourhood is not causally privileged.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service availability omits Nederweert's canal/drainage, A2/care and operator-state dependencies.
notes: The 189 HWH assets and four local Waterinfo observations remain display context and do not drive catchment, gate/pump, receiving-level, power/backup or recession state.
NWB balances only logical Mobility and Supply through N275/N266; it does not represent A2 gateway, canal crossing, bus, external care acceptance or operator networks.
Provider areas, one planning sample, antenna/school registers and one indicative air observation do not calibrate availability, occupancy, backup or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic contribution ledgers reconcile, but public evidence and operational action provenance do not support the displayed local precision.
notes: Hazard/service contribution sums and counterfactual records remain inspectable.
At T+24 river output reports legacy depth 0.753195, 1,913 affected residents and 87,036 person-hours; this is deterministic scenario arithmetic, not an authority observation or forecast.

The Groningen earthquake has zero local ground motion, severity and affected residents but still accumulates 1,053 person-hours at T+24 and 1,909 at T+72; any burden is indirect synthetic network scope, not local earthquake damage.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 plateaus, deterioration and recovery are not driven by a confirmed Nederweert action/resource ledger.
notes: River depth stays 0.753195 while affected residents rise 1,913→2,311 and burden 87,036→355,296 from T+24 to T+72; Facilities alone falls 0.812602→0.697501 without a selected arrival, isolation, care or relief action.

Compound depth remains about 0.194/0.193 while affected residents move 6,068→5,872 and burden 155,100→596,291; seven services stay near their degraded T+24 values and Facilities changes 0.449675→0.525478 without governed intervention state.

No public record establishes support-site opening, pump/gate switching, fire suppression, generator/fuel deployment, road priority, care acceptance, sheltering, water distribution, resupply or verified restoration completion.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, centre containment, regional membership and resident reconciliation are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 plus audit:context verify GM0946/Nederweert/Limburg/VRLN, the contained reference point and a three-resident (+0.017%) neighbourhood rounding difference reconciled deterministically.
findings.action: Retain the 2025 source edition, exact official nulls, deterministic reconciliation and separate BAG/BRT semantics.

findings.summary: Nine active hazard/component families reuse one source-blind fifteen-neighbourhood surface.
findings.evidence: Diagnostics/model inspection show one common scenario seed and neighbourhood-ID hash drive local hazardSeverity regardless of water path, wind, heat, cyber origin or smoke plume; a controlled Ospeldijk ignition does not create source-contained affected population.
findings.action: Suppress local consequence maps until each mechanism samples a governed event footprint; test source containment, hydraulic/fuel geometry and cross-hazard rank divergence.

findings.summary: Persistent major-river stress is not a selected, connected Nederweert flood mechanism.
findings.evidence: At T+24/T+72 the model holds depth 0.753195 while affected residents rise 1,913→2,311 and burden 87,036→355,296. E03/E04/E07 identify local channels, streams, structures and observations, but none supports the generic depth, footprint or time course.
findings.action: Require a selected LIWO/authority hydraulic event that proves a connected Maas/canal/stream pathway, boundary/datum, structure state, footprint, arrival/recession, uncertainty and licence; otherwise direct local consequences remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Pluvial output ignores Nederweert's official priority, road, storage and Bientje drainage evidence.
findings.evidence: At T+24 rainfall is zero while residual depth is 0.186709, affected residents zero and burden 44,691 person-hours. E03 maps T=10/Herwijnen areas, road blockage and storage/overflow; E04 documents recurring Bientje inundation and the culvert to Neerpeelbeek.
findings.action: Bind event rainfall to AHN/BGT flow, municipal stress-test geometry, road sags, sewer/ditch/channel/culvert topology, storage, controls, power and recession; render missing state Unknown.

findings.summary: Canonical and controlled wildfire tests do not represent De Groote Peel or Weerterbos consequence pathways.
findings.evidence: The remote canonical ignition yields GM0946 smoke 0.186439, no flame and zero affected at T+24. Moving ignition to Ospeldijk yields city flame 0.362249/smoke 0.394695 but still zero affected and no containing-neighbourhood precedence, despite E03/E05 identifying real peat/heath/woodland fuel and management areas.
findings.action: Use versioned fuel/moisture, wind/plume, access, compartment/barrier and suppression inputs for De Groote Peel and Weerterbos; keep planning measures separate from completed/live state.

findings.summary: Partial water-control registers and local observations are visible but non-causal.
findings.evidence: E07 exposes 189 points with every capacity null plus four current local Waterinfo station records. Registered existence and a point measurement establish neither topology, catchment, remaining capacity, control, power/backup nor T+72 performance.
findings.action: Integrate authority-approved GWSW/Waterschap topology and valid-time aggregate control/state where publishable; otherwise keep context affectsSimulation=false and Water/Drainage synthetic or Unknown.

findings.summary: N275/N266 links omit the explicit A2 gateway and canal-crossing workflow.
findings.evidence: E06 shows two N275 series edges and one N266 edge; nominal 150 values are scenario ceilings. Provincial evidence identifies exit 39/N275–A2 as a key gateway and continuing N275 works, while the graph has no gateway/crossing object, direction, live incident or detour state.
findings.action: Model N275 once as a physical corridor, add A2 junction and N266/canal-crossing dependencies, and gate route/care/supply workflows on valid-time NDW/operator state or explicit synthetic assumptions.

findings.summary: Facilities availability hides cross-boundary acute-care route and acceptance dependence.
findings.evidence: E06 finds no acute hospital inside; St. Jans Gasthuis in Weert is about 5.6 km straight-line away. The model has no origin-route-destination travel, junction/crossing state, ambulance capacity, diversion, staff, surge, backup or acceptance.
findings.action: Represent care as a time-valid origin-route-destination workflow and retain unobserved acceptance, staffing, occupancy, backup and restoration as Unknown.

findings.summary: Provider areas, capacity planning and facility registers cannot calibrate exact service availability.
findings.evidence: E08 identifies regional Enexis/WML roles, overlapping point-territory results, one NEDW planning sample, 37 antenna sites and eight schools, but no physical connectivity, current load/flow/quality/outage, backhaul, backup, staff, stock or repair state. Drainage territory is empty despite 189 real water assets.
findings.action: Label percentages as synthetic; ingest only authorised timestamped aggregate outage/restoration data, preserve topology/security limits, and never turn no-match or overlap into zero/coverage.

findings.summary: Sparse observations require explicit space/time/coverage semantics.
findings.evidence: E07/E08 provide four canal points and one indicative air station but zero local fixed KNMI weather stations, Waterinfo forecasts, acute-care points, government-service points, NDW situations and seismic origins. Current points do not supply a continuous field or scenario horizon.
findings.action: Show point location, time, quality, units and coverage; prohibit silent interpolation/projection and render absent disciplines NoData rather than normal water/weather, clean air, open roads or safety.

findings.summary: Correct narrow zeros and indirect effects still need explicit scope labels.
findings.evidence: Direct coastal depth and Groningen-earthquake ground motion are zero, but coastal wind/service burden and earthquake person-hours remain from synthetic wider-network effects; the wildfire preset is remote smoke. None should be described as local coastal inundation, shaking damage or observed plume.
findings.action: Retain supported direct zeros only within named source scope, label indirect network/smoke consequences separately and never infer all-hazard safety.

findings.summary: First-72-hour deterioration and recovery lack accountable local actions and resources.
findings.evidence: River and compound service/affected/burden trajectories change through T+72 without selected interventions. E08 defines possible emergency-power and drinking-water actions but no GM0946 activation, locations, capacities, staff, stocks, fuel or completion state.
findings.action: Add a timestamped T0–6–12–24–48–72 action/resource/blocker ledger; suppress recovery attribution and operational site/count claims where authority state is unavailable.

corrections.summary: Replace GM0946's generic river/pluvial fields with selected connected canal/stream and rain–terrain–drainage events while retaining narrow direct-coastal zero.
corrections.validation: Assert source event, connected waterbody/catchment, boundary/datum, structure state, footprint, issue/valid time, arrival/recession, uncertainty/licence and NoData; unsupported affected/service/recovery renders Unknown.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared local seed with mechanism-specific footprints, including De Groote Peel/Weerterbos wildfire source containment.
corrections.validation: Water, wind, heat, smoke and cyber use distinct evidence-backed surfaces; a controlled eligible Ospeldijk ignition affects its containing region before unrelated areas and cross-service physical hazard remains invariant.

corrections.summary: Govern Nederweert's canal, surface-water and sewer chain without converting registers or current point observations into live/future performance.
corrections.validation: Source/version/licence/coverage and capacity nulls persist; only connected unit-compatible valid-time gate/pump/culvert/sewer/control/backup state affects services, and current observations never project to T+72.

corrections.summary: Represent N275/N266, the A2 exit-39 gateway, canal crossings, buses and St. Jans acute-care access as non-additive time-valid workflows.
corrections.validation: N275 series edges never add capacity; junction/crossing closure propagates once to eligible Mobility/Supply/care routes; live state and destination acceptance remain Unknown when absent.

corrections.summary: Make first-72-hour service and recovery changes depend on confirmed or visibly synthetic actions, resources and blockers.
corrections.validation: Every T0/6/12/24/48/72 change cites incident, actor, action, resource, valid time and constraint; absent support site, stock, staff, fuel, shelter, care, water distribution or restoration is Unknown.

residualLimitations: No inspected public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Enexis/WML/gas/telecom/sewer/canal-control topology, current state, backup endurance, priority users, crews or restoration estimates.
No governed public catalogue supplies GM0946 emergency-support locations with live opening, staff, stocks, fuel, shelter capacity, care acceptance or completed first-72-hour actions.
HWH aggregation is partial and every local capacity field is null; registered existence is not operating state and no unlisted asset may be inferred absent.
Municipal climate and nature-fire documents are planning/context evidence, not incident probability, current fuel/water state, depth, response or completion.
Four Waterinfo points and one indicative air station retain point/time validity only; zero local forecast/weather/road/care/seismic matches are scoped NoData.
Dynamic workers, visitors, road/canal users, school/care/shelter occupants and responders are absent from resident exposure.
NWB nominal capacities are generalized scenario units; no conclusion about real junction, crossing, evacuation or supply throughput is supported.
Exact local hazard, affected, service, person-hour and recovery values remain synthetic until an authority-reviewed event and operational action ledger are bound.
provinceReviewFlags: Coordinate one connected Limburg major-river/canal/tributary scenario family; do not independently tune generic municipality depths without hydraulic connectivity and defence/control state.

Review Noordervaart, Zuid-Willemsvaart, Kanaal Wessem-Nederweert, Neerpeelbeek, Bientje, Rietbeek and local sewer/ditch dependencies across Nederweert, Weert, Someren and Peel en Maas in flood and drought modes.
Coordinate De Groote Peel with Brabant-Zuidoost/Asten-Someren and Weerterbos-Hugterheide with Cranendonck; retain fuel, compartments, access and implementation lifecycle separately.
Audit N275/N266, A2 exit 39 and canal crossings once as shared physical corridors; deduplicate N275 series edges and propagate common-cause closure to bus, supply and care workflows.
Coordinate St. Jans Gasthuis Weert and alternative Roermond/Brabant acute-care origin-route-destination capacity instead of assigning generic local Facilities percentages.
Require Limburg-wide NoData rules for sparse KNMI/RIVM/RWS/NDW observations, provider overlaps and partial HWH registers; nearest/empty coverage is never a municipality value or all-clear.
Review the shared seeded neighbourhood surface and unsupported T+72 action/recovery assumptions as national model issues rather than accepting municipality-specific tuning.
